sentences.text:
By way of this application under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (hereinafter referred to as "the Code"), the petitioner has prayed for quashing and setting aside FIR being C.R.No.I - 5 of 2012 registered with Detroj Station, for the offences punishable under Sections 406,
420, 272, 273, 114 of the IPC as well as all other consequential proceedings arising out of the aforesaid FIR qua the petitioner herein.

2. Seeking quashment of the FIR, learned advocate, Mr. NR Kodekar appearing for the petitioner,
referring to the judgement of the Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Ram Nath Vs. State of UP and others, (2024) 3 SCC 502, would submit that the Food Safety And Standards Act, 2006 (in short "the Act") came into effect from 29th July 2010 gives overriding effect to NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/14443/2013 ORDER DATED: 08/07/2025 undefined any other law, including IPC and CRPC.

sentences.text: Thus filing of the FIR and subsequently charge sheet is abuse of process of law, since by overriding effect of the Act, the prosecution under the IPC is not maintainable for selling adulterated Ghee and further the trial against the accused is abuse of process of law.

He would further submit that no Food Inspector was present when the sample was taken, no procedure under the provisions of the Act was followed, and therefore it cannot be said that article i.e. Ghee was substandard.

He would further submit that even if the allegation made in the FIR is believed to be true, the whole incident fall under the four corners of the Act and the Act having been special Act by reading sections 48 and 89 of the Act, it governed the issue and therefore, the prosecution under the IPC is not maintainable.
Upon such submission, learned advocate Mr. Kodekar prays to allow this petition and to quash the FIR as well as the charge sheet filed against the petitioner.

3. On the other hand, learned APP appearing for the State vemently objecting to the relief claimed by the petitioner would submit that the charge is already framed by the learned trial Court at Exh.18 under sections 406, 420, 272,273 and 114 of the IPC.

He would further submit that the petitioner was not only adulterating Ghee, but was selling the same in the open market by labelling it as Vasant Shuddh Ghee, Girnari Shuddh Ghee, Sopan Shuddh Ghee, Astha Shuddh Ghee etc. and thereby, was cheating the society at large.

He NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/14443/2013 ORDER DATED:
08/07/2025 undefined would further submit that sample, which was collected during the raid, has been sent to the FSL and the report thereof indicates that the Ghee is adulterated.

He would further submit that since the charge is already framed in the matter without making any resistance and that no relief is claimed to challenge the framing of the charge, present petition under section 482 of the code is not maintainable.

Lastly, he would submit that this is the fourth offence to the credit of the petitioner and all the offences are of similar in nature and thus, looking to this aspect, it is submitted not to allow the petition and to dismiss the same.
4. The substance of the allegations reads as under:-
"The applicant-accused herein, i.e. Shaileshkumar Natvarlal Bhatt, address - Rampura, Detroj, current address - 106, B2, Vishvas Flats, Sola Road, Thaltej,
Ahmedabad, has been caught from a food factory namely Shri Kunteshwar Dairy and Food Products on at 16:30 hours on 29/01/2012, wherein the accused in the present case, in collusion with each other, used to adulterate soyabean oil and vegetable-ghee with essence-color, i.e. chemical substance, to alter it as ghee and thereafter, the accused used to pack the adulterated substance in various tins and pouches labeled as Shuddh Ghee of brands such as Shri Gopi, Vasant Suddh Ghee, Shri Girnar Sopan Astha etc. and used to sell the adulterated substance in the market and thus,
committing breach of trust with the customers who used to buy such items.

On 29/01/2012, the accused No. (1) Jashvantsinh Ganpatsinh Solanki, residing at Bhagaji Na Muvad, Taluka Kapadvanj, District Kheda and accused No. (2) Shailesh Vakhatisinh Chauhan, residing at Bhati, Taluka Dahegam, District Gandhinagar have been caught from the place along with the Muddamal having aggregated value of Rs.
10,68,800/-, i.e. NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/14443/2013 ORDER DATED:
08/07/2025 undefined different size of packets of adulterated substance and Sailesh Natvarlal Bhatt vs State Of Gujarat on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70505579/

sentences.text:
Whereas the accused No. (3) Manubhai Atmaram Chauhan, residing at Bhati, Taluka Dahegam, District Gandhinagar and the present applicant, i.e. Accused No. (4) Shaileshkumar Natvarlal Bhatt, residing at Rampura, Taluka Detroj, at present residing at 106, B2, Vishwas Flats, Sola Road,
Thaltej, Ahmedabad came to be caught later.

The accused have committed a breach of trust with the public by adulterating edible material and selling it as Suddha Ghee in the open market and thus, committed an offence."
5.

Upon above alleged facts of the case, the learned trial Court in Criminal Case No.490 of 2012 framed the charges at Exh.18, which reads as under:-
"Shri Kunteshwar Dairy and Food Products is situated at village Rampura, wherein the accused, in collusion with each other, used to used to adulterate soyabean oil and vegetable-ghee with essence-color, i.e. chemical substance, to alter it as ghee, package the adulterated substance in various tins and pouches labeled as Shuddh Ghee of brands such as Shri Gopi, Vasant Suddh Ghee, Shri Girnar Sopan Astha etc. and used to sell the adulterated substance in the market and thus, committing breach of trust with the customers, i.e. buyers of such items.

On 29/01/2012, the accused No. (1) and accused No. (2) were caught from the place along with the Muddamal having aggregated value of Rs. 10,68,800/-, i.e. different size of packets of adulterated substance and equipment used in food adulteration.
Whereas the accused No. (3) and accused No. (4) came to be caught later.

The accused have committed a breach of trust with the public by adulterating edible material and selling it as Suddha Ghee in the open market and thus, committed an offense punishable under Section 406, 420,
272, 273, 114 of I.P.C. in the jurisdiction of this Court."
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/14443/2013 ORDER DATED: 08/07/2025 undefined 6.
The solitary contention of Learned advocate for the petitioner is that in view of Section 89 of the Act, the offence under the IPC is now not maintainable.

Looking to the facts noted hereinabove, it appears that the petitioner was knowing fully well that he is manufacturing adulterated Ghee, sold it under the different names and thereby cheated the public at large, therefore prima facie offence under sections 406 and 420 of the IPC are established.
7. Heavy reliance was placed upon the judgement of Ram Nath (supra), where the offence under sections 272 and 273 of the IPC was sought to be quashed.

The Hon'ble Apex Court has held that section 59 of the Act will be attracted and the offence under the said Act is more stringent than the offence under Sections 272 and 273 of the IPC and on this ground, while considering section 89 of the Act, the Hon'ble Apex Court has quashed the FIR.
In that matter, it was a case of selling mustard oil without license.
The facts of the present case are quite distinct and different from the fact of that case.

Moreover, the petitioner submitted himself to frame the charge without any resistence and thereafter, suddenly wake up from slumber to challenge the entire proceedics by way of filing present petition.
Thus, the judgement cited by learned advocate for petitioner renders no help to his case.

sentences.text: This Court is quite conscious that power u/s 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 is extraordinary power and should be used sparingly, as the exercise of such power would scuttle the FIR at the threshold.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/14443/2013 ORDER DATED: 08/07/2025 undefined 9.

At the cost of repetition, it can be said that the petitioner is knowing fully well that he is manufacturing adulterated Ghee with an intent to cheat the public at large and society and sold it under the different names in the market.
Even the FSL report indicates that the sample taken from the factory of the petitioner is found to be adulterated.
Therefore, looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, the proceedings under the IPC against the petitioner in the present case is maintainable.

10. In the case of State of Haryana Vs. Bhajanlal & ors., AIR 1992 SC 604, the Hon'ble Apex Court has opined that power of quashing can be exercised very sparingly and that too in rarest of rare case.

entities.text: State of Haryana Vs. Bhajanlal & ors., AIR 1992 SC 604
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Relevant observations reads as under:-
"103.

We also give a note of caution to the effect that the power of quashing a criminal proceeding should be exercised very sparingly and with circumspection and that too in the rarest of rare cases; that the court will not be justified in embarking upon an enquiry as to the reliability or genuineness or otherwise of the allegations made in the FIR or the complaint and that the extraordinary or inherent powers do not confer an arbitrary jurisdiction on the court to act according to its whims or caprice."
11. In the result, present petition fails and stands dismissed.
Rule discharged.
Interim relief granted earlier stands vacated.
